tweet_summary: A video asks why 'so many athletes suddenly stopped wearing wireless headphones', implying they did so because Bluetooth/EMF radiation is a health threat ('the biggest threat to public health').
why_note_decision: There is no evidence of a widespread shift of athletes away from Bluetooth for health reasons; the premise rests on a few anecdotes (e.g. an Aaron Rodgers joke). Public-health bodies (WHO etc.) find wireless earbuds emit low non-ionizing RF well below safety limits with no established cancer/neurological link. The video (846K-follower account, 877K impressions) promotes EMF health misinformation, so a correction is warranted. I disagree with the provisional no-note because this is a checkable, misleading health claim with real reach.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note (1) states there is no evidence athletes have broadly abandoned Bluetooth for health/radiation reasons, and (2) notes that wireless earbuds emit low-level non-ionizing RF below regulatory safety limits with no established link to cancer or brain harm, citing a credible health authority/fact-check. It must avoid endorsing the EMF-danger premise. A note that validates the radiation-health-threat claim, or merely says 'athletes prefer wired', without addressing the false health premise should FAIL.
reference_note: Misleading - there's no evidence athletes have abruptly abandoned Bluetooth for health reasons. Public health agencies say wireless earbuds emit low non-ionizing RF below safety limits and aren't linked to cancer; choices often come down to battery, fit or convenience. https://www.health.com/condition/cancer/bluetooth-wireless-headphones-cancer https://blackdotresearch.sg/have-professional-athletes-stopped-using-bluetooth-wireless-headphones-due-to-radiation-and-electromagnetic-fields-being-emitted-from-them/

fact_check.claim_verdict: misleading - no evidence of a health-driven abandonment of Bluetooth; RF from earbuds is non-ionizing, below safety limits, no established cancer/brain-harm link
fact_check.notes: Fact-checks: no widespread shift away from Bluetooth; trend stems partly from an Aaron Rodgers joke. WHO/Healthline/Reuters find no confirmed link to cancer; Bluetooth emits 10-400x less RF than phones. Wired preferences are usually battery/fit/convenience.

importance.lens_rationale: 877K impressions from a large account spreading EMF/anti-wireless health fear; correcting science-denial health misinformation has clear public-health value.
